text:
maria: Quick follow-up to the ephemeral-route RFC — two practical questions: how should the allocator handle transient spikes (burst from CI/onboard) vs sustained overuse, and how do we tie that to per-tenant egress budgets for billing/alerts?

kevin: I think we need a two-tier policy: a short burst allowance (token-bucket) plus a moving-window sustained limit. bursts shouldn't evaporate other tenants but sustained leaks should trigger eviction and throttling.

alex: +1. Also we need a clear signal to the control plane so routers can start applying backpressure early (instead of waiting for eviction). Maybe a controller-exported header or circuit-breaker metric?

sam: Suggestion: controller exposes two signals per-tenant: `ephemeral_available` (tokens left) and `ephemeral_state` (OK|THROTTLED|EVICTING). Routers poll metrics or scrape and act. For long-term accounting, increment a counter that feeds the billing pipeline.

kevin: Implementation sketch: allocator keeps an in-memory token-bucket (burst / second) and a sliding-window counter (5m avg). On restart we persist bucket state to a lightweight Lease CRD so we don't lose cheap tokens during quick controller restarts. If sustained > threshold -> transition to EVICTING state and start LRU eviction with a short TTL.

maria: Curious about durability tradeoffs. Persisting every token update seems heavy. How coarse can we make it and still be useful?

kevin: We persist only on state transitions and periodic checkpoints (every 30s) — not every token hop. That gives us eventual accuracy and avoids API thrash. Roots of truth for billing will be the counters (which we persist per-tenant to the metrics DB).

alex: For backpressure, can we add an opt-in HTTP header `X-Redwood-Egress-Mode: best-effort|budgeted` so SDKs can choose how they fall back? If budgeted -> SDKs gracefully reduce QPS when `ephemeral_state=THROTTLED`.

sam: That works. Also propose an admin API to set soft vs hard limits per tenant and a webhook for alerts when moving to EVICTING so CS can reach out.

kevin: Minor ops note: eviction ordering should prefer oldest ephemeral allocations and allocations without recent activity. Implement as a TTL sweep + LRU queue. We should avoid cross-tenant preemption.

infra-bot: FYI deploy: allocator-controller v0.18 rolled to staging at 1729995300, will enable `ephemeral_metrics` flag for testing.

maria: Action items: 1) kevin to write operator spike (Lease CRD + checkpointing) 2) sam to add metrics + webhook prototype 3) alex to draft SDK header proposal and fallback semantics. Ping me on PRs.

kevin: I'll open a spike PR today with a tiny Lease CRD and a local simulator.

sam: I'll throw together a Grafana panel and alert rule.

maria: Thanks — let's reconvene after the spike results. :thumbsup:
